conviction_note: Revenue, cash use and cash were pre-released on 15 Oct, so the print turns on what was NOT given: the Q4 setup (implied Q4 revenue ~$280-287m, +25-27% y/y and +44% q/q, to hit the 15-16% FY guide, plus the positive-EBITDAS-in-Q4 target the 15 Oct release left out) and the quality of the 'record low' $28m cash use, which contains ~$47m of asset-sale receipts. Those lean mildly negative, but every one of them is an inference from company documents rather than an unseen number, against ~21% of shares sold short (5.7 days) and a call-heavy book (put/call OI 0.08), so p_up sits at 46 on an abs move of 9% (option-implied 12.4% net, trimmed because the quarter is pre-released). The findings sum to -1.6, the scaled number is -0.72; the gap is the crowded short and the inference-grade evidence, which reach p_up rather than the per-finding sizes.
bar: Revenue bar disputed across three estimate sources: $193.33m (Seeking Alpha, https://seekingalpha.com/news/4668473-plug-power-q3-2026-earnings-preview-company-analysts-optimistic), $195.4m (Earnings Whispers, https://finviz.com/news/413857/plug-powers-turnaround-faces-a-credibility-test-as-shares-sink-toward-lows), $198.2m (Investing.com, https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/plug-power-earnings-on-deck-as-hydrogen-firm-eyes-profitability-93CH-5012562); EPS -$0.06 to -$0.07. Company pre-release says revenue grew >10% on Q3 2025's $177.06m, i.e. >~$194.8m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926115964/tm2627628d1_ex99-1.htm). No gross-margin consensus found. The bar the stock actually trades on is the FY2026 guide of ~15-16% revenue growth (on $710m FY2025) and the positive-EBITDAS-in-Q4-2026 target (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926093339/tm2622713d1_ex99-1.htm). Because the revenue bar is disputed, findings on the reported revenue line are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 291.96M shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, ~5.7 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/plug, read 2026-11-09); 284.62M at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 5.8 days (same aggregator via search). Shares outstanding 1,397,195,278 as of 2026-08-06 (10-Q cover, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926093454/plug-20260630x10q.htm), so short ~21% of shares outstanding: a crowded short, trend down from 330M (July) and 294M (August). Baseline: 25d skew null (not computed), put/call open-interest ratio 0.08 (extremely call-heavy, retail-long book), ATM IV 146.9%, event-implied move 12.44%, ATM spread 18% of mid. Tape: +14.1% over 5 sessions on a sector-wide fuel-cell rebound after the midterms (no company news), -7.7% over 20 sessions, -63.9% from 52w high, 14% off the 52w low. A crowded short plus a call-heavy book means a squeeze mechanism exists on any positive surprise; every negative below was shrunk for it.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of ~15-16% growth on FY2025's $710m implies $816-824m; Q1 $163.5m + Q2 $178.3m + Q3 ~$195m (>10% on $177.06m) = ~$537m, so Q4 must be ~$280-287m, +25-27% y/y on Q4 2025's $225.2m and ~+44% sequentially, with the CFO saying in August that 'the majority of the volume in the second half ... we expect to unfold in the fourth quarter' (mostly electrolyzer equipment, whose timelines the 15 Oct release itself says 'vary'); the call either reaffirms that back-end load or trims it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-03-02 print with a positive Q4 gross margin and an FY2026 growth outlook moved +23.2%; the 2026-08-10 print that RAISED the FY guide to 15-16% moved +5.21%; the 15 Oct pre-release reaffirming 'on track' moved +2.76%. Guidance raises have been bought; no recent trim to compare.
findings.why_not_priced: The pre-release reaffirmed the guide in one line and gave no Q4 number, so the wire carries 'on track' without the implied +44% q/q Q4 that a trim would visibly reprice; if the market doubted the guide the Q3 consensus range ($193-198m) and the FY consensus would sit below the guide, and the previews (Earnings Whispers 2026-11-02) flag the Q4 weight only qualitatively. The 12.4% implied move says a big Q4 surprise either way is possible; it does not say which.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 base and FY2025 $710m from the March 2026 results coverage (https://www.renewable-energy-industry.com/news/world/article-7268-plug-power-stock-takes-off-plug-power-increases-2025-revenue-to-710-million-and-achieves-positive-gross-margin-in-q4); Q1 2026 $163.5m (https://www.renewable-energy-industry.com/news/world/article-7418-plug-power-boosts-q1-revenue-significantly-and-improves-margins-targets-positive-ebitdas-by-end-of-2026-stock-climbs); CFO Q4-weighting quote from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15420770575819776); Earnings Whispers preview says ~10% Q3 growth 'would put heavy weight on Q4' (https://finviz.com/news/413857/plug-powers-turnaround-faces-a-credibility-test-as-shares-sink-toward-lows). Shares the Q4-deliverability theme with the EBITDAS finding but rests on different numbers (revenue, not cost).

findings.finding: The positive-EBITDAS-in-Q4-2026 target, reaffirmed on the Q2 call ('we remain on track'), was not mentioned in the 15 Oct pre-release, and the arithmetic is steep: Q2 gross margin was about -0.9% and Q2 opex of $62m was flattered by a $37m one-time contract recovery (run rate ~$75m per Earnings Whispers), so Q4 needs a gross margin in the mid-teens or better on ~$283m revenue; a softened or re-dated target is the most likely negative in the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The EBITDAS target has been reaffirmed at every print since Q4 2025 (March +23.2%, May +1.14%, August +5.21%); it has never been withdrawn, so there is no reaction on a softening to cite. In November 2025 the stock fell -1.17% on the print and slid afterwards with the target pushed to 'Q4 2026'.
findings.why_not_priced: The omission is in a release the wire summarised as 'on track'; the target itself is still quoted in previews as live (Benzinga/Investing 2026-11-09). If the market had priced a slip, the stock would not have rallied 14% into the print and the previews would not frame Q4 EBITDAS as the 'key test'. It is an inference from wording plus arithmetic, not a company number, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 opex one-off and run-rate from Earnings Whispers (https://finviz.com/news/413857/plug-powers-turnaround-faces-a-credibility-test-as-shares-sink-toward-lows); Q2 reaffirmation in the call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15420770575819776); Q2 gross loss $1.7m in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926093339/tm2622713d1_ex99-1.htm). Related to the Q3 gross-margin wording finding (both about margin trajectory) but on a different quarter and line.

findings.finding: The 'record low' Q3 net cash usage of ~$28m (unrestricted cash $161.9m at 30 Jun to ~$134m at 30 Sep) includes the ~$47m of Graham, Texas / Gateway asset-monetization proceeds the CFO said were received in July-August, plus scheduled restricted-cash releases (~$155m due over 12 months), so the underlying burn is on the order of $70m+ a quarter against $134m unrestricted cash; the 10-Q cash-flow statement will show operating cash flow, and the company's own liquidity plan leans on 'available equity programs' (ATM/SEPA).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash-use improvement has been the line the stock bought: Q2's $61m (-58% q/q) print moved +5.21%, the 15 Oct $28m 'record low' pre-release +2.76%. In November 2024 a going-concern disclosure on ~$111m unrestricted cash crashed the stock (https://www.power-eng.com/operations-maintenance/plug-power-casts-substantial-doubt-over-its-ability-to-survive-amid-cash-crunch/).
findings.why_not_priced: The pre-release headlined net usage and did not split operating burn from asset-sale receipts; the 'record low' framing was bought (+2.76%). If the market had decomposed it, the cash-use line would not be cited as the turnaround's proof point in every preview. Financing question asked per rule: the money funds operating losses, not a visible order ramp, so the sign is negative; sized small because the receipts are disclosed and an analyst can do the subtraction.
findings.independence: Q2 release confirms $161.9m unrestricted cash and $47m received in July-August (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926093339/tm2622713d1_ex99-1.htm); 15 Oct 8-K gives $134m and $28m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926115964/tm2627628d1_ex99-1.htm); a secondary Q2 summary says the absence of the DOE facility increases reliance on ATM and SEPA (https://www.panabee.com/news/plug-power-earnings-q2-2026-report). EDGAR shows no 424B5 or new equity filing between 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-09 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001093691&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40).

findings.finding: The 15 Oct pre-release says the company 'has demonstrated gross margin improvement over the past two quarters' and expects 'continued year-over-year progress' in Q3, a YoY comparison against a Q3 2025 GAAP gross margin of about -67.9%, rather than a sequential claim against Q2's ~-0.9%: hedged wording that leaves room for a sequential step back in Q3 margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has been the line the stock re-rated on: the first positive gross margin (Q4 2025, +2.4%) moved +23.2%; Q1 2026's -13% (+42pp y/y) moved +1.14%; Q2's ~breakeven +5.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote the sentence as 'margins improved, further progress expected' without noting the YoY base; no gross-margin consensus was found, so nothing anchors a sequential expectation. An inference from wording only, so it is sized small; a sequential improvement would remove it.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 gross loss ~$120m on $177m (-67.9%) from the Q3 2025 8-K coverage (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465925109120/tm2530762d1_ex99-1.htm); Earnings Whispers notes fuel margin 'stalled sequentially' in Q2 (https://finviz.com/news/413857/plug-powers-turnaround-faces-a-credibility-test-as-shares-sink-toward-lows). Shares the 15 Oct document with findings on cash and revenue.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is pre-released at >10% y/y on $177.06m, i.e. above ~$194.8m, against a disputed consensus of $193.3m / $195.4m / $198.2m: roughly in line, with no surprise left on the headline line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 beat revenue ($178.3m vs $168.8m) and moved +5.21%; the pre-release itself moved +2.76%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: pre-released 25 days ago. Filed at near zero because the exact figure could land a few million above the low consensus; capped small because the bar is disputed.

findings.finding: Part of the $275m+ asset-monetization plan, the $142m New York Gateway sale to Stream, needs New York State environmental and regulatory review for its non-land closing (long-stop extended to 2027-03-31), while Governor Hochul's Executive Order 62 (effective 2026-07-14) pauses discretionary environmental permits for data centers of 50 MW or more for up to a year; any call update on Gateway timing bears on the non-dilutive liquidity path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 Stream deal announcement is not in the baseline's print history; no prior call update on Gateway to cite.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the moratorium and the extended long-stop were public in July and coverage flagged the uncertainty. Residual is what the call says about timing; a confirmed delay to 2027 would make the ATM path more likely before the March long-stop.
findings.independence: Moratorium terms (https://www.bdlaw.com/publications/new-york-enacts-first-statewide-moratorium-on-data-centers/) and the governor's office 2026-10-06 transcript saying the permit pause continues for up to a year (https://governor.ny.gov/news/b-roll-video-audio-photos-rush-transcript-governor-hochul-and-representatives-ocasio-cortez). Overlaps the liquidity theme of the cash-burn finding, but on a different, future cash source.

findings.finding: Positioning: 291.96M shares short at the 2026-10-15 settlement (~21% of 1.397bn shares outstanding, ~5.7 days to cover), an open-interest put/call ratio of 0.08 and a +14.1% five-session sector rebound into the print; any clean reaffirmation of the Q4 EBITDAS target or the FY guide meets a crowded short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +23.2% March 2026 reaction came with short interest in the mid-20s% (Invezz reported 25% in January 2026, https://invezz.com/news/2026/01/05/plug-power-stock-faces-elevated-risks-as-short-interest-hits-25/); the July 2026 short interest of 27.4% preceded a squeeze-style rally (https://invezz.com/news/2026/07/08/plug-power-stock-sinks-even-as-turnaround-story-builds-short-interest-hits-274percent/).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, so the level is known; what is not priced is the conditional: the shorts are positioned for the Q4 targets to slip, so a reaffirmation forces covering. The trend in short interest (330M July to 292M October) shows covering already under way, which caps this.
findings.independence: Prior settlement 284.62M / 5.8 days (Sept 30) per aggregator search; share count from the 10-Q cover (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926093454/plug-20260630x10q.htm); sector-driven run-up per https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/unternehmensnachrichten/plug-power-s-9-5-prozent-friday-pop-sentiment-got-it-there-but-the-cash-burn-will-decide-what-sticks/70477017

findings.finding: Electrolyzer order flow the call can convert to backlog: a 280 MW GenEco supply agreement with Arcadia eFuels (Project ENDOR, Denmark) plus a >1 GW preferred-supplier cooperation, a 50 MW Orica order post-FID, Barrow Green's remaining 25 MW expected to reach FID in 2026, and the 275 MW Courant FEED (FID early 2027); an ~$8bn funnel with no backlog figure ever given.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order announcements were in the 15 Oct release (+2.76%); H.C. Wainwright cited the Arcadia deal in keeping a $7 target while Morgan Stanley cut to $1.20 in October.
findings.why_not_priced: The orders are in the wire; what is not is a dollar backlog, which the company has never given. A first backlog number or the Barrow Green FID on the call would be new. Small because the Courant FID and most of the funnel resolve after the window.
findings.independence: Q2 call on Barrow Green and Courant timing (https://www.webull.com/news/15420770575819776); analyst views from https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/plug-power-earnings-on-deck-as-hydrogen-firm-eyes-profitability-93CH-5012562

findings.finding: COO Dean Fullerton resigned effective 2026-10-23 'to accept a position at another company', duties spread across EVPs and VPs; the call is the first since his departure, ahead of the Q4 ramp he would have run operationally.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior executive-departure reaction in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since September; mostly priced. Residual only if the call shows the Q4 execution plan without an operations lead.

findings.finding: Sector backdrop: renewables and hydrogen names rallied after the 2026 midterms on coverage tying it to preservation of the 45V hydrogen production credit for projects that begin construction by January 2028, and fuel-cell peers (FuelCell Energy, Bloom Energy) rose with PLUG on 2026-11-06 without company news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced in the +14% five-day run-up; macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed, so filed small. Management commentary on 45V eligibility for customer projects is the residual.
findings.independence: Search summary of the 2026-11-04 premarket coverage linked the move to 45V preservation (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/11/63036949/plug-power-fuels-up-ahead-of-earnings-tonight-heres-what-investors-need-to-know, 403 on fetch, snippet_only).

outside_window.finding: Plug Symposium 2026 (virtual, 2026-11-19, 09:00-12:00 ET) is where strategy or longer-range outlook may be presented, which could hold back 2027 commentary from the 9 Nov call.
New York Gateway non-land closing long-stop 2027-03-31, inside New York's one-year data-center permit pause; the $142m itself resolves after the window.
Courant 275 MW (Quebec) final investment decision estimated early 2027.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filings 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-09: no 424B5, S-3 or equity-raise filing after the 15 Oct 8-K; only Forms 4/144 (small 10b5-1 sales) and the COO 8-K
Q2 2026 10-Q liquidity/going-concern text: the filing fetch truncated before MD&A; EDGAR full-text search confirms 'at-the-market' language in the 10-Q but the capacity/usage could not be read

Gross-margin consensus for Q3: none found in four previews

rejected_candidates.candidate: GAAP EPS likely swings on mark-to-market of convertibles ($578m) and warrants ($136m liability at 30 Jun); last quarter's charge was $104m, and the share price fell over Q3, which would point to a non-cash gain
rejected_candidates.detail: No sourced 30 Jun and 30 Sep share prices to size the remeasurement; one_off below operating income in any case, near-zero weight

rejected_candidates.candidate: CSO Benjamin Haycraft sold 9,375 shares at $1.41 on 2026-10-15 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-06-11
rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into positioning context; a pre-planned sale of ~$13k carries no information about the print

baseline_tension: The mild negative lean (Q4 back-end load, an omitted EBITDAS target, a flattered cash line) cuts against a call-heavy book, a 21% short base already covering and a +14% five-day run-up; with no skew number to lean on, the crowded short is the reason p_up sits at 46 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, ~21% of shares, 5.7 days): shrank every negative (Q4 revenue -1.0 to -0.8, EBITDAS -1.5 to -1.0, cash burn -1.0 to -0.8, margin wording -0.8 to -0.5, Gateway -0.5 to -0.3, COO -0.2 to -0.1) and raised the positioning finding +1.0 to +1.2; p_up 45 to 46

Rule 5 (documents beat inference): the EBITDAS and margin-wording findings are inferences from wording and arithmetic, kept small; the cash-burn finding rests on the company's own disclosed receipts and kept most of its size
Rule 6 (disputed bar, three estimates $193-198m): reported-revenue finding capped at +0.2
Rule 4 (financing is a question): asked what the cash buys; it funds operating losses, not a corroborated order ramp, so the cash finding stays negative

Rule 3 (read the set): Q4 revenue and Q4 EBITDAS share the Q4-deliverability theme but rest on different numbers, kept separate and said so in independence; Gateway timing beyond the call moved to outside_window
